scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.speaker: Rose
scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.text: \Raya do Pastrana Park. \Ga \tikang \iya ro mga \tawo kon \agahon.
scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.translation: This is Pastrana Park. People walk here in the mornings.

scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.speaker: Player
scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.text: It's nice here. Peaceful, unlike the busy streets in the States.

scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.speaker: Rose
scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.text: Wait until festival season. Not peaceful at all then. But that's later.

scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.speaker: Rose
scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.text: Nong Pedring said he'd meet us here. He sells at the market, he's our suki.

scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.speaker: Rose
scene_1_pastrana_park_morning_walk.text: I don't see him, though. Help me look, balikbayan? Ask around the park. Someone here has to be him.

scene_1_found_pedring.speaker: Player
scene_1_found_pedring.text: Excuse me... are you Nong Pedring?

scene_1_found_pedring.speaker: Nong Pedring
scene_1_found_pedring.text: I am! And you must be Jonabel's apo, the one from abroad. Where's Rose?

scene_1_found_pedring.speaker: Player
scene_1_found_pedring.text: Rose! Over here, I found him!

ask_pedring_passerby.speaker: Player
ask_pedring_passerby.text: Excuse me, are you Nong Pedring?

ask_pedring_passerby.speaker: Passerby
ask_pedring_passerby.text: \Bukon. The market vendors usually wait on the south side, by the street.

ask_pedring_passerby.speaker: Passerby
ask_pedring_passerby.text: Haha, \bukon! I'm just out for a walk.

culture_parish_priest.speaker: Parish Priest
culture_parish_priest.text: Welcome, child. This is the Cathedral of Saint John the Baptist, the seat of the Diocese of Kalibo.

culture_parish_priest.speaker: Parish Priest
culture_parish_priest.text: Saint John is Kalibo's patron. His feast is June 24. But look at the altar: most hearts here belong to the Santo Niño.

culture_parish_priest.speaker: Parish Priest
culture_parish_priest.text: The Santo Niño is the Holy Child Jesus. This cathedral is also his diocesan shrine.

culture_parish_priest.speaker: Parish Priest
culture_parish_priest.text: Every January, on the third Sunday, Kalibo honors him with the Ati-Atihan. Drums, painted faces, the whole town dancing in the streets.

culture_parish_priest.speaker: Parish Priest
culture_parish_priest.text: They shout "Hala bira!" and "Viva Señor Santo Niño!" all day, then come here to pray and give thanks.

culture_parish_priest.speaker: Parish Priest
culture_parish_priest.text: The dancing and the praying go together here. That is Aklan's devotion.

examine_santo_nino.text: An image of the Santo Niño, the Child Jesus, in a rich robe and crown. He holds a globe and a scepter.
Candles and fresh flowers have been left in front of him.

culture_park_martyrs.speaker: Lola Ising
culture_park_martyrs.text: You're new here, \apo? Come, sit a while. Do you know what happened in this park?

culture_park_martyrs.speaker: Lola Ising
culture_park_martyrs.text: In the revolution against Spain, Aklan's fighters were led by Francisco del Castillo. He died in March 1897, and his marker stands here in Pastrana.

culture_park_martyrs.speaker: Lola Ising
culture_park_martyrs.text: A few days later, on March 23, nineteen men from Kalibo, Malinao and Lagatik were shot by the Spanish.

culture_park_martyrs.speaker: Lola Ising
culture_park_martyrs.text: We call them the Nineteen Martyrs of Aklan. They rest at the Aklan Freedom Shrine. Everybody just calls it "Castillo."

culture_park_martyrs.speaker: Lola Ising
culture_park_martyrs.text: So when you walk through Pastrana, walk a little slower. Brave people stood here.

choices.label: Hey, it's okay. What's your name?
Are you lost?

lost_child.speaker: Bea
lost_child.text: I was with my Lola, then she was gone. She has a pink umbrella.

lost_child.speaker: Player
lost_child.text: Stay right here by the fountain, Bea. I'll find her.

lost_child_lola.speaker: Bea's Lola
lost_child_lola.text: Have you seen a little girl? My \apo, Bea. I turned around and she was gone!
lost_child_lola.translation: Have you seen a little girl? My grandchild, Bea. I turned around and she was gone!

lost_child_lola.speaker: Player
lost_child_lola.text: She's by the fountain. She told me her name.

lost_child_lola.speaker: Bea's Lola
lost_child_lola.translation: Thank you, apo! Thank you, thank you.

scene_1_meet_pedring.speaker: Rose
scene_1_meet_pedring.translation: That's Nong Pedring. He's our regular vendor at the market.

scene_1_meet_pedring.text: Will you talk to Nong Pedring?

choices.label: Mayad nga agahon! I'm Jonabel's grandchild.
Uh, hi. Sorry, I'm still nervous speaking Akeanon.
I'll just wait here, you go ahead.

scene_1_meet_pedring.speaker: Nong Pedring
scene_1_meet_pedring.translation: Good morning to you too! So you're Jonabel's grandchild. Where are you from?

scene_1_meet_pedring.speaker: Nong Pedring
scene_1_meet_pedring.translation: Don't be nervous. Slow only. Learning takes time, apo.

scene_1_meet_pedring.speaker: Rose
scene_1_meet_pedring.text: Suit yourself. But you'll have to talk to people eventually.

scene_1_meet_pedring.speaker: Nong Pedring
scene_1_meet_pedring.translation: Come by the market, you two.

scene_1_meet_pedring.speaker: Nong Pedring
scene_1_meet_pedring.translation: Wow, all the way from abroad!

scene_1_meet_pedring.speaker: Rose
scene_1_meet_pedring.translation: That's where we'll learn the names of things.

scene_1b_food_words.speaker: Rose
scene_1b_food_words.text: Before we go in. You'll want these.

scene_1b_food_words.speaker: Rose
scene_1b_food_words.text: \Isda — fish. \Manok — chicken. \Itlog — egg. \Bugas — rice. \Tinapay — bread. \Karne — meat. \Baboy — pig.

scene_1b_food_words.speaker: Player
scene_1b_food_words.text: Okay, that's a lot of food words. Good thing we're going in right now.

scene_1b_food_words.speaker: Rose
scene_1b_food_words.text: Exactly why I taught them now. Use it or lose it, balikbayan.

scene_1b_food_words.speaker: Rose
scene_1b_food_words.text: Not bad. Now try them on a real vendor.

scene_1b_food_words.speaker: Rose
scene_1b_food_words.text: Close enough. You'll hear every one of them inside.

scene_2_kalibo_public_market.text: The market is full of color and noise — fruits, fish, cloth, everything mixed together. The smell of dried fish and freshly cooked rice fills the air.

scene_2_kalibo_public_market.speaker: Rose
scene_2_kalibo_public_market.text: Go on, look around. Talk to me when you are done.

scene_2_market_talk.speaker: Nong Pedring
scene_2_market_talk.translation: What would you like, apo? There's plenty here: rice, water, dried fish.

scene_2_market_talk.speaker: Player
scene_2_market_talk.text: Rose, how do I say I want this?

scene_2_market_talk.speaker: Rose
scene_2_market_talk.text: Say "\pangabay" first. Means please. Basic manners, balikbayan.
Player points at a round, ridged yellow fruit.

choices.label: Yes, pangabay, I'd like to try it.
Maybe later, let me look around first.
I'm okay, I'm not a fan of exotic fruits, sorry.

scene_2_market_talk.speaker: Nong Pedring
scene_2_market_talk.text: That's fine, my goods won't disappear quickly.

scene_2_market_talk.speaker: Rose
scene_2_market_talk.text: Your loss. This is literally one of the best things here.

scene_2_market_talk.speaker: Nong Pedring
scene_2_market_talk.translation: Where are you off to next? To church?

scene_2_market_talk.speaker: Rose
scene_2_market_talk.text: Then "\it \daya", this one. He's older, so add "\Nong" and "\ho". Point when you say it.

scene_2_market_talk.prompt: Ask Nong Pedring for the fruit.

scene_2_market_talk.speaker: Nong Pedring
scene_2_market_talk.translation: Wow! Did you hear that, apo?

scene_2_market_talk.speaker: Rose
scene_2_market_talk.translation: May I have this one, Nong, please. Again, slowly.

scene_3_kalibo_cathedral_midday.text: A large church, strong walls, people going in and out — everyday life, not just for festivals.

scene_3_kalibo_cathedral_midday.speaker: Rose
scene_3_kalibo_cathedral_midday.text: Take your time, balikbayan. Talk to me when you are ready.

scene_3_cathedral_talk.speaker: Lola Susan
scene_3_cathedral_talk.translation: Back then, we all always went to church here. Your Lola Jonabel most of all, she was the most devout.

scene_3_cathedral_talk.speaker: Lola Jonabel
scene_3_cathedral_talk.text: (laughs) Don't believe her, \Apo. We were all equally naughty back then.
The group sits outside the church, Rose holding a town map.

scene_3_cathedral_talk.speaker: Rose
scene_3_cathedral_talk.text: \Hara, tan-awa. \Mapa it Kalibo. Kon \magtuon ka it mga \lugar, mas \madali ka \makaagto bisan siin.
scene_3_cathedral_talk.translation: Here, look at this. Map of Kalibo. If you learn the places, you'll find your way anywhere more easily.

scene_3_cathedral_talk.text: What will you say to Rose?

choices.label: This is actually really helpful. Saeamat, Rose.
I'll try to remember the names, no promises though.
A physical map? Can't I just use my phone?

scene_3_cathedral_talk.speaker: Rose
scene_3_cathedral_talk.text: See, not completely hopeless after all.

scene_3_cathedral_talk.speaker: Rose
scene_3_cathedral_talk.text: That's more effort than I expected, honestly.

scene_3_cathedral_talk.speaker: Rose
scene_3_cathedral_talk.text: Sure, and when your phone dies, then what, balikbayan?

scene_3_cathedral_talk.speaker: Lola Susan
scene_3_cathedral_talk.text: We'll go ahead home. Don't keep them out too long, Rose.

scene_4_souvenir_shop_invite.speaker: Rose
scene_4_souvenir_shop_invite.text: Before we go home, there's a little souvenir shop right by the cathedral. Come, let's take a look.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.text: Inside, the little souvenir shop is packed with colorful items. Rose stops for another practice round.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.text: Round two. \An-om, \pito, \waeo, \siyam, \napueo — six through ten. Finish counting to ten this time.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.text: Now, colors — look at everything on these shelves.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.text: \Puti — white. \Itom — black. \Puea — red. \Asul — blue. \Dueaw — yellow. \Berde — green.

choices.label: I like the puea one — the red one. It really stands out.
Maybe the puti, the white one. Simple.
Honestly, I can't tell half these colors apart yet, sorry Rose.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.text: Good eye. Bold color for a bold first attempt at counting.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.text: They'll stick eventually. Nobody gets it all at once.
Rose holds up a small basket, then a big one.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.text: \Daya — "this." \Duyon — "that," near us both. \Dato — "that," farther away. Point when you say it, it's easier.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.text: Not so fast. Let's see if you know what they mean.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.text: Almost. Say them again on the way home.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.text: Now let's test your eyes. Look at each color and tell me its name.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.text: Good. You know your colors now.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.text: Not bad for a first try. Look at the shelves again on your way out.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_number.text: That's enough for one day. Let's go home, balikbayan.

scene_0_home_atlast.speaker: Lola Susan
scene_0_home_atlast.text: That flight must have worn you all out. Go on upstairs and sleep in your rooms.

scene_0_home_atlast.speaker: Lola Susan
scene_0_home_atlast.text: Look next to the doors. Yours is the one with the \bituon.
scene_0_home_atlast.translation: Yours is the one with the star.

scene_0_home_atlast.speaker: Lola Susan
scene_0_home_atlast.text: Jonabel has the \buean, and Jobert has the \adlaw.
scene_0_home_atlast.translation: Jonabel has the moon, and Jobert has the sun.

scene_0_home_atlast.speaker: Rose
scene_0_home_atlast.text: Rest up, balikbayan. When you're up tomorrow, come find me. I'll show you the town.

scene_5_evening_home.speaker: Lola Jonabel
scene_5_evening_home.text: So, \apo. What did you like best today?
What do you tell Lola Jonabel?

choices.label: The cathedral. Lola Susan says you were the most devout.
The market. So much food.
Honestly? It was hot. I mostly wanted to sit down.

scene_5_evening_home.speaker: Lola Susan
scene_5_evening_home.text: Wait until Sunday. After mass, the market is even busier.

scene_5_evening_home.speaker: Rose
scene_5_evening_home.text: You sat on every bench in Kalibo, balikbayan. Every one.

scene_5_evening_home.speaker: Lola Jonabel
scene_5_evening_home.text: I used to sit on those church steps after mass. I'd forgotten how loud the bells are.

scene_5_evening_home.speaker: Lola Jonabel
scene_5_evening_home.text: There's one more place I'd like you to see. Another day.

scene_5_evening_home.speaker: Rose
scene_5_evening_home.text: Another trip, another day. Don't get comfortable, balikbayan.

scene_5_evening_home.speaker: Lola Susan
scene_5_evening_home.translation: On Sunday, we go to mass. All of us.

scene_5_evening_home.speaker: Rose
scene_5_evening_home.text: You don't even know what day it is, do you, balikbayan?

scene_5_evening_home.speaker: Rose
scene_5_evening_home.translation: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday.

scene_5_evening_home.speaker: Rose
scene_5_evening_home.text: They are. Free points for you. Now prove it.

scene_5_evening_home.speaker: Rose
scene_5_evening_home.text: You have until \Domingo to learn them.

scene_0b_ask_rose.speaker: Lola Susan
scene_0b_ask_rose.text: \Mayad nga \agahon! There you are! Did you sleep well?
scene_0b_ask_rose.translation: Good morning! There you are! Did you sleep well?

scene_0b_ask_rose.speaker: Lola Susan
scene_0b_ask_rose.text: Whenever you want to look around, always ask Rose to go with you.

scene_sunday_mass_invite.speaker: Lola Susan
scene_sunday_mass_invite.text: It's Sunday! Rose and I are going to the cathedral for mass, then to the market after.

choices.label: Sure, I'll go with you.
Maybe another time.

scene_sunday_mass_invite.speaker: Lola Susan
scene_sunday_mass_invite.text: Good! Let's go before all the seats are taken.

scene_sunday_mass_invite.speaker: Rose
scene_sunday_mass_invite.text: Suit yourself. We'll be back by noon.

scene_sunday_mass_invite.speaker: Lola Susan
scene_sunday_mass_invite.text: Your Lola Jonabel is staying home today. Keep her company, \apo.

choices.label: Can you show me around?
Not right now

scene_rose_walk_to_park.speaker: Rose
scene_rose_walk_to_park.text: Finally. Let's start with the park. Stay close.

choices.label: Can we go out again?
Not right now

scene_rose_walk_to_park.speaker: Rose
scene_rose_walk_to_park.text: Back to the park, then. Stay close.

choices.label: Can we go out again?
Can we see the mangroves at Bakhawan?
Not right now

scene_rose_walk_to_park.speaker: Rose
scene_rose_walk_to_park.text: The Bakhawan mangrove forest? Good pick, there's a long bamboo boardwalk through the trees. Stay close.

choices.label: Can we go out again?
Can we see the mangroves at Bakhawan?
Can we go to the weavers?
Not right now

scene_rose_walk_to_park.speaker: Rose
scene_rose_walk_to_park.text: Back to Manang Loleng's. She'll put you to work again. Stay close.

scene_rose_not_now.speaker: Rose
scene_rose_not_now.text: Not now, balikbayan. Ask me in the morning.

scene_mass_market.speaker: Lola Susan
scene_mass_market.text: That's everything. Let's go home before the food gets cold.

lines.speaker: Nong Pedring
lines.translation: Buy some fish, apo, it's still fresh.

lines.speaker: Nong Pedring
lines.text: Your Lola Susan has been my \suki for thirty years. Don't tell her I said thirty.

lines.speaker: Nong Pedring
lines.text: Another star fruit, \apo? I kept the sweetest one for you.
